reason: Tool-surface cost work on code.server.tool#11 produced rules no existing skill states: which verbs list before registration (Verb.needs_project), which tools take project and layers (Module.layered), how the cost is measured, and the test pitfalls. metaform-mcp-connect-budget covers connect text only, so a new class-level skill is the right home.

Adding a dispatch write verb required a registry entry in test_mcp's UNSEEN_OPEN_WORLD, and that test already fails on other sessions' entries, so the failure must be attributed by name. The skill's test bullet does not mention the registry.

Module.layered was removed the same day it was added (too coarse, per the orchestrator); the skill still names it in its trigger. The new per-verb flags are Verb.needs_project, Verb.reads_layers and Verb.listed, so the trigger must name them to route the next session here.

Per-verb reads_layers, Verb.listed state gating and the description cut rule are now how tools are listed; the skill's bullet still describes module-level layered=True, which no longer exists, so a future session would add the wrong flag.
The measurement run this episode used checks.py with the argument after, in the critic's layout; measure.py was not the script used to produce the before and after figures.
Verb flags, listing checks and the registry test are the metaform-module-capability-checklist Verbs section; the measured table moved to references/tool-surface-measure.md.
